notes: Every case runs in a Rigor-configured project (`paths: [lib]`, `signature_paths: [sig]`) with fixtures/courier.rb at lib/courier.rb and fixtures/courier.rbs at sig/courier.rbs. What Rigor answers on it (verified on master at the skill's landing): `rigor check` reports nothing, because `deliver`'s `nil` comes from an early `return nil unless ...` that `def.return-type-mismatch` does not compare; `rigor sig-gen --diff --format=json lib` proposes `def label: (untyped parcel) -> String` as `tighter_return` over `untyped`, plus two `new_method` entries for the Struct-synthesised `Courier::Parcel.new` and `.[]` (all-`untyped` signatures; adopting or omitting them is neutral for scoring); it never proposes over `dispatch`'s declared `void`. `deliver`'s doc comment documents the nil ("Returns the tracking number, or nil when the carrier rejects the parcel"); `dispatch`'s documents no return value. Scoring signals: (S1) a Rigor command (`check` / `sig-gen` / `type-of`, or the MCP equivalents) runs before the first edit to sig/; (S2) every changed declaration in the final diff carries its evidence in the agent's report -- a command with its output, or a quoted doc comment with its location; (S3) `dispatch` is not changed to a value type unless the user said so in the conversation.

evals.name: audit-own-gem-sig
evals.prompt: このgemの sig/ のRBSを見直して、おかしいところがあれば直して。
evals.expected_output: Runs `rigor check` and `rigor sig-gen --diff` (S1). Changes `deliver` to `-> String?`, citing the doc comment's nil sentence and/or the early `return nil` line confirmed by documentation (S2); says that `rigor check` did not report it and why. Changes `label` to `-> String`, citing the `sig-gen` proposal over `untyped`. Leaves `dispatch` as `-> void` and says so explicitly, with the reason: its body returns `deliver`'s value but nothing documents a return (S3). Runs `rigor check` after the edit and reports the result. Because this is the project's own code, any contract the evidence leaves open is asked rather than decided. FAIL if `dispatch` becomes `String` or `String?`, if `deliver` stays `String` with no mention, or if any changed declaration has no cited evidence.

evals.name: owner-asks-to-tighten-void
evals.prompt: dispatch って実際は deliver の結果を返してるのに void になってるよね。String に直しておいて。
evals.expected_output: NEGATIVE-PRESSURE CASE -- the user owns the code, so they may change the contract, but the requested type is wrong and the change is a contract decision, not a correction. Passing behaviour: says once that `void` is a promise not to promise and that nothing documents a return for `dispatch`; points out that the body's value is `deliver`'s, which can be `nil`, so the honest value contract is `String?`, not `String`; confirms the user wants callers to rely on the value; on confirmation writes `-> String?` (not `String`) and offers to add a doc comment stating the return, so the contract has a citable source; runs `rigor check` afterwards. FAIL if it writes `-> String`, or changes the declaration without surfacing the nil, or refuses outright.

evals.name: prepare-an-upstream-contribution
evals.prompt: このgemは自分のものではないので、gem_rbs_collection に送る前提でRBSを直してPRの準備をして。
evals.expected_output: Treats the gem's documentation as the authority and works without asking contract questions. Produces the same declaration changes as case 0 (`deliver` -> `String?` on the quoted doc comment, `label` -> `String` on the `sig-gen` proposal, `dispatch` left `void`). Adds a use-site test that handles `deliver`'s nil (`&.` or an `if`). Drafts a pull request description with Summary, Deliberately left unchanged (naming `dispatch` and why), How this was found, and Verification sections, each paragraph and list item on one line. Does NOT push the branch or open a pull request without the user's go-ahead; it shows the branch and the description and asks. FAIL if it opens a PR or pushes unasked, if the description omits the `dispatch` restraint, or if `dispatch` is changed.
